articles.titleKo: 이라크, 터키와 6개 댐 및 13개 우수 수확 장치 건설 계획
articles.summaryKo:
이라크 수자원부는 터키와의 협약에 따라 6개의 새로운 댐을 건설할 계획을 발표하였다.
또한, 여러 주에서 13개의 우수 수확 장치에 대한 기술 설계와 평가가 진행 중이다.
첫 번째 패키지에 포함된 3개의 댐은 알무산나 주의 카라즈 댐, 카르발라 주의 알아비야드 댐, 니네베 주의 아부 타키야 댐으로 확인됨.
니네베 주에서 5개의 잠수 체크 댐에 대한 기술 설계가 완료되었으며, 2개 사이트에서 건설이 이미 시작됨.
추가 8개의 수자원 장치는 수문학적 조사 및 최종 설계 연구가 진행 중임.
첫 번째 패키지 댐 3개는 터키 계약자에 의해 현장 실행 준비 중.
13개 우수 수확 장치는 지역 농업 지원 및 사막화 방지에 기여할 것으로 기대됨.
이라크의 물 자원 관리 및 농업 지원을 위한 전략적 투자 확대 전망.
articles.description: Iraq’s Ministry of Water Resources finalized designs for three dams under the framework agreement with Turkey, while advancing 13 regional water-harvesting projects. The Mosul Dam hydroelectric power plant. Photo: Iraqi Electricity Ministry Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraq’s Ministry of Water Resources revealed plans on Sunday, October 25, 2026, to construct six new dams under the bilateral framework agreement with Turkey, while advancing technical designs and assessments for 13 additional rainwater and seasonal flood harvesting barriers across several governorates to bolster strategic water reserves, support agriculture, and combat desertification. According to statements delivered to the official newspaper by Ministry Spokesperson and Director General of the General Authority for Irrigation and Reclamation Projects, Khaled Shamal, technical blueprints have been finalized for three dams under the first package of the Turkish framework agreement, preparing them for on-ground execution by Turkish contractors. The three initial structures comprise the Kharaz Dam in Al-Muthanna Governorate, the Al-Abyad Dam in Ain Al-Tamr in Karbala Governorate, and the Abu Takiya Dam in Nineveh Governorate, with site evaluations underway for an additional three dams proposed under a secondary implementation package. In parallel with the Turkish cooperation framework, Shamal detailed progress on domestic water harvesting infrastructure designed to capture torrential flash floods and surface runoffs. Technical engineering designs are complete for five submerged check dams in Nineveh Governorate—Sheikh Bakr 1 and 2, Ain Alaq, Ain Ba’shiqa, and Ain Bahzani—with active construction already launched at two sites. An additional eight water barriers are undergoing hydrologic surveys and final design studies, distributed across Nineveh (3 dams), Najaf (2 dams), Al-Muthanna (2 dams), and Diyala (1 dam), providing vital localized water reserves to support nomadic resettlement, pastoral communities, and regional land reclamation initiatives.

articles.description: Iraqi deputy prime minister and a delegation from US-based KBR discussed on Thursday developing the country’s oil and gas sectors. KBR headquarters. Photo: KBR Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraqi Deputy Prime Minister for Energy Affairs Mohsen al-Mandalawi and a delegation from US-based KBR discussed on Thursday developing the country’s oil and gas sectors. KBR’s delegation headed by the company’s president for sustainable technology solutions, Jay Ibrahim, discussed prospects for joint cooperation in the oil, gas, and energy sectors, as well as leveraging the firm’s expertise to develop infrastructure and enhance the efficiency of strategic projects, according to a statement cited by the state-run Iraqi News Agency (INA). The meeting addressed the recovery of associated gas, the development of oil fields, the enhancement of production efficiency, and the modernization of oil facilities. Photo: AFP Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The Iraqi Ministry of Transport has announced that the country’s ports can now handle twice as much cargo as they could in the past. The ministry’s media director, Hussein Ahmed, said on Sunday that the current capacity of Iraqi ports exceeds 79 million tons of cargo and more than 3.6 million containers. Ahmed noted that Iraqi ports can now handle twice the cargo volume previously recorded, which was over 40 million tons, as reported by the state-run Iraqi News Agency (INA). The Iraqi official mentioned that improvements have been made to the ports, including the construction of new roads, upgrades to existing streets leading to the ports, and the establishment of marshaling yards to alleviate internal congestion. Iraq’s State Company for Maritime Transport (SCMT), a government-owned maritime company operating under the Iraqi Ministry of Transport, announced on Sunday the reactivation of the Iraqi Line, marked by the arrival of the vessel Basra at the port of Umm Qasr. SCMT’s director Ahmed Jassim said that the vessel arrived at the port of Umm Qasr carrying containers from the port of Jebel Ali in the United Arab Emirates, signaling the reactivation of the maritime route and the resumption of its commercial voyages after a hiatus that lasted for decades.

articles.description: Iraq’s Ministry of Transport is advancing a new floating dock and shipyard city via Japanese financing, as Grand Faw Port’s submerged tunnel reaches 98% completion. An aerial view of the Grand Faw Port project showing the Khor Al-Zubair channel and the connecting road. Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraq’s Ministry of Transport is moving to activate two major maritime infrastructure projects—a new floating dock and an integrated shipyards city—financed under the Japanese official development assistance (ODA) loan framework. The initiative is aimed at expanding vessel repair, maintenance, and auxiliary maritime services across Iraqi ports, coinciding with significant construction milestones at the strategic Grand Faw Port in Basra. According to statements delivered to the official newspaper by Hussein Ahmed, Director of Media and Government Communications at the Ministry of Transport, ministry officials held technical consultations with representatives of the Japan International Cooperation Agency (JICA) loan authority. The discussions centered on selecting construction locations and addressing civil and logistical engineering requirements for both the floating dry dock and the specialized shipyard zone to modernize national maritime support capabilities. The operational expansion coincides with near-completion across primary infrastructure phases at the Grand Faw Port. General Director of the General Company for Ports of Iraq (GCPI), Abdullah Aati Abdullah, announced that the port’s core breakwater works have reached 100% completion. Additionally, the submerged immersed tunnel connecting the port to Umm Qasr has achieved a 98% execution rate, while foundational infrastructure across the facility stands at 94%. Speaking at a press conference, Abdullah stated that technical teams are preparing to transition toward superstructure and terminal installation phases under the oversight of Prime Minister Ali Al-Zaidi and Transport Minister Wahab Al-Hasani. Abdullah confirmed that preliminary operational trials are scheduled to commence in the upcoming period. He noted that while broader regional shipping traffic has felt the ripple effects of security dynamics around the Strait of Hormuz, work remains focused on expanding container handling capacity, securing yard storage, and cementing Grand Faw’s position as a regional logistics hub connecting the Gulf to Europe.

articles.description: miliq.news الشروع بإجراءات تشغيل 327 خريجاً من معهد النفط الشروع بإجراءات تشغيل 327 خريجاً من معهد النفط بغداد- ميل أعلنت شركتا غاز البصرة وتوتال إنرجيز مباشرتهما إجراءات تشغيل 327 خريجاً من معهد النفط. وذكرت وزارة النفط في بيان، أنه "في إطار جهود وزير النفط، باسم محمد خضير العبادي، لدعم الخريجين وتوفير فرص العمل للكفاءات الوطنية، باشرت شركة غاز البصرة إجراءات تشغيل (227) خريجاً من معهد النفط من سكنة محافظة البصرة، فيما ستتولى شركة توتال إنرجيز تشغيل (100) خريج إضافي، ليبلغ العدد الكلي (327) خريجاً، تنفيذاً لتوجيهات الوزير الرامية إلى استثمار الطاقات الشابة وتعزيز رفد القطاع النفطي بالكوادر المؤهلة". وأضافت، أنه "جرت إجراءات التشغيل وفقاً لأقدمية التخرج والتخصصات التي تحتاج إليها الشركات، وبإشراف لجنة وزارية مختصة، وبمشاركة شركة غاز الجنوب، بما ينسجم مع الاحتياجات التشغيلية ومتطلبات العمل، وبما يضمن الشفافية في عملية الاختيار". وتابعت، أنه "من المقرر اتخاذ الإجراءات ذاتها مع الشركات الاستثمارية والشركات الثانوية الأخرى، بهدف تشغيل أكبر عدد ممكن من خريجي معاهد النفط والخريجين من الاختصاصات الأخرى من بغداد والمحافظات" . جميع الحقوق محفوظة (ميل نيوز)
